written.myAnswer: Xylem transports water and dissolved mineral salts; phloem transports food.

The root has an outer epidermis bearing root hairs, a cortex, an endodermis at the inner boundary of the cortex, a pericycle, and central vascular tissues (xylem and phloem). Root hairs absorb mineral salts by active transport and water by osmosis. Water and dissolved salts pass through the epidermis, cortex, endodermis, and pericycle into the xylem.
